annotationRationale: The logarithm power rule reduces the equation to one variable, and the inverse exponential relation recovers three positive values of a for each base. The multiplication principle counts the pairs.

review.mathCheck: Every allowed base exceeds 1, so u=log_b(a) ranges bijectively over the reals. Factoring gives u=0 or u=±2017^(1/2016), exactly three real values. Their inverse images satisfy b^(−r)<1<b^r. There are 199 bases, including both endpoints, yielding 3×199=597 distinct ordered pairs, choice E.
